subject: Re: Evaluation success signals — workbook + edge-case validation plan
messages:
From: Sophia Li <sophia@healthops.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Kumar <rajiv.k@healthops.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: HealthOps evaluation — kickoff and MAP draft

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Rajiv and I pulled together a quick Mutual Action Plan (attached) and a set of concerns we want validated during the pilot. High level: we need to ensure precision on extraction tasks, stable 99th-percentile latency under 350ms for API calls, and an audit trail for inference requests (retention 90 days).

Could you confirm whether Redwood can provide:
- a runnable acceptance test matrix the SE team can execute each sprint
- an exportable audit log sample for our security team
- a smoke-validation sequence to run during cutover

We proposed a 3-week evaluation window (11/2–11/20) in the MAP but are flexible if Redwood recommends a different cadence. Attaching the MAP (HealthOps_MAP_v1.xlsx) and a short list of edge-case scenarios.

Thanks — look forward to aligning on exit gates.

Best,
Sophia
VP Product, HealthOps

Attachments: HealthOps_MAP_v1.xlsx, edgecase-acceptance-tests.csv
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Sophia Li <sophia@healthops.com>
Cc: Rajiv Kumar <rajiv.k@healthops.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-13T09:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HealthOps evaluation — kickoff and MAP draft

Hi Sophia — thanks for the MAP and the scenario list, this is a great start.

High level response: yes, we can provide an executable acceptance test matrix and an audit log export. Below are the concrete proposals for Success Signals and Exit Gates we recommend including in the MAP workbook:

1) Functional acceptance (pass/fail per test):
- Extraction accuracy: F1 >= 0.88 on 3 canonical datasets + 5 edge cases from your file.
- Reranking precision: top-1 relevance lift >= 15% vs baseline for the sample prompts.

2) Non-functional exit gates:
- Latency: p95 < 220ms, p99 < 350ms for 2k concurrent-ish calls (synthetic workload).
- Error budget: < 0.5% 5xx rate during the run window.

3) Security & compliance:
- Audit log extract: one-week sample with request-id, model-version, and KV-cache hit/miss flagged.
- Data residency check: inference payloads not persisted beyond 90 days (configurable).

4) Cutover smoke tests: (we'll provide an automated script)
- Token-level cost sanity check, smoke prompt run, verification of trace ids, and drive export.

Attached: I exported a starter test matrix (edgecase-acceptance-tests.csv) and a one-page smoke checklist (smoke-test-checklist.pdf).

Proposed timeline:
- Week 0 (now–10/20): finalize MAP and acceptance matrix
- Week 1 (10/21–10/27): test harness setup + baseline runs
- Week 2 (10/28–11/3): partner-run evaluation (scheduled tests)
- Week 3 (11/4–11/10): stabilization + final verification -> signoff target 11/12

If you prefer the 11/2 start, we can compress the baseline step but will need additional SE hours.
I'll loop Karthik and Marissa for the technical runbook and the script delivery.
—Camila
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference

Attachments: edgecase-acceptance-tests.csv, smoke-test-checklist.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Sophia Li <sophia@healthops.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-14T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HealthOps evaluation — kickoff and MAP draft

Thanks — adding a few technical acceptance items from the runtime/ops side that should be explicit in the MAP:

- Model pinning: evaluation must run against immutable model artifact (model v3.1.2) to avoid drift during the run.
- KV cache warming: verify cold-start vs warmed-path token delta < 12% latency overhead.
- Quantization parity: for any 8-bit candidate we recommend a 1k prompt concordance check (acceptable drift threshold 3% for entity extraction).
- Fallback policy: define automatic fallback target (cheaper variant) and the acceptable performance delta when fallback engages.

Operational hooks we'll provide:
- Continuous tracing ids in every API response header (x-rw-trace)
- Live cost telemetry per-request (for spike detection during runs)

On the timeline: Karthik notes that the 10/21 baseline runs require access to a dedicated slot; we'll reserve a Dedicated pool for 10/21–10/27 if HealthOps confirms. That reservation is typically a small commit but will guarantee capacity for p99 measurements.

I'll prepare a short runbook with commands and expected outputs for the SE team to execute.

-Karthik
Principal Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sophia Li <sophia@healthops.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-16T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HealthOps evaluation — kickoff and MAP draft

Sophia — attaching a compact SE runbook and the smoke-test script we'll hand off. Key items included in the runbook:

- Pre-flight checklist (IAM roles, API keys, model pin config, dataset access)
- Smoke test steps (curl examples):
  1) POST /v1/generate with sample prompt A -> expect entity list + trace id
  2) Bulk-run 100 concurrent prompts with ramp to 500/s -> capture p95/p99
  3) Run edge-case set (from your CSV) and record F1 per scenario

- Acceptance reporting template: pass/fail, artifact links, test seed, and verification steps.

I'll upload the script to the shared Drive folder and can run the baseline on 10/21 morning US-PST if you give us a 2-hour window and temporary test credentials.

Note: Neha will coordinate the audit log sample export for your security team.

Thanks,
Marissa
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachments: se-runbook.md, smoke-test-checklist.pdf
From: Sophia Li <sophia@healthops.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Rajiv Kumar <rajiv.k@healthops.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HealthOps evaluation — kickoff and MAP draft

Team — this looks good and actionable. A few clarifying asks before we lock dates:

- Can Redwood guarantee a model-pinning artifact and a way to replay runs against the pinned artifact post-eval? Our compliance team needs reproducibility for 6 months.
- For the audit log sample, can you include an anonymized payload sample showing request-id, model-version, and response latency? That will satisfy our SOC reviewer.
- If we go with your compressed timeline (11/2 start), we request a daily 30-minute sync for the first week to quickly triage failures.

If Redwood can confirm the reproducibility and provide the anonymized log sample by COB 10/22, we will sign the MAP and confirm the dedicated slot.

I'll sign off internally on the 10/21 baseline reservation if you can provide the SE window and the short runbook you mentioned.

Best,
Sophia
VP Product, HealthOps
